difficulty.from: The Climb tier 9 of 10 (this bank has no per-item difficulty)

answer.line: Ionization energy rises across period 3, but it dips twice: at Al and at S.

steps: Here is the trend: across a period, more protons pull on the same shell, so first ionization energy rises.
Dip 1, Mg to Al. Al loses an electron from 3p, which sits higher than Mg's filled 3s. Easier to remove, so Al comes in under Mg.
Dip 2, P to S. P has three unpaired 3p electrons. S has to pair its fourth, and that repulsion makes one easier to pull off.
Put both dips into the rise: Al (578) < Mg (738) < Si (786) < S (1000) < P (1012), in kJ/mol.

choices.note: The rising trend with both dips in place.
This is the plain left-to-right rise. It pulls because it is the rule you learned first. This item tests both exceptions.
It has the s-to-p dip at Al but misses the pairing dip at S.
It has the pairing dip at S but misses the dip at Al.
This is the plain trend read in decreasing order, which is also the size order. The stem asks for increasing.
